claim: A WNT/regeneration-associated biological state is a cross-sectional AGA state candidate supported by two transcriptomic contexts plus an orthogonal human protein/localization/perturbation study; it is not a validated actuator-response or recoverability coordinate.

transcript_context_1.result: WNT/regeneration-loss direction positive in 5/5 paired subjects

transcript_context_2.result: WNT/regeneration-loss positive mean; 4/6 gene directions aligned

orthogonal_human_mechanism_state.source: Lu et al. 2016; PMID 27472703; PMCID PMC5265840
orthogonal_human_mechanism_state.human_material: 15 male AGA patients; 15 frontal balding specimens and 9 occipital nonbalding specimens
reported_observations: lower Wnt10a and LEF1 mRNA in balding follicles
higher TGF-beta1 protein/pathway activity in balding follicles
TGF-beta inhibition increased Wnt10a/LEF1 and beta-catenin nuclear translocation in balding DP cells
Wnt inhibition in nonbalding DP cells increased active TGF-beta1 and Smad2/Akt phosphorylation

state_response_boundary.result: the frozen cross-sectional transcript projection failed its pre-registered monotonic short-term response prediction
state_response_boundary.invariant: State Separation Axis != Actuator Response Axis

evidence_topology.interpretation: the orthogonal study removes the frozen transcript-axis definition as a single point of failure for the broad R-state compatibility claim

open_defeaters: R_state remains an abstract latent candidate rather than a directly measured scalar
cross-sectional and ex-vivo/cell perturbation evidence does not establish longitudinal human recoverability
the orthogonal source still studies Wnt/TGF-beta family biology and is not independent of the broader mechanistic hypothesis
measurement-family independence does not imply cohort or causal independence

next_bridge.preferred: human or human-follicle intervention-linked study measuring an early orthogonal internal response and a later functional/hair output
next_bridge.high_value_source_candidate: 2026 human AGA organ model, PMID 42237333, which links DHT input, growth/catagen/proliferation/apoptosis, molecular state, and partial pharmacologic reversal
next_bridge.reason: move from cross-sectional state compatibility toward response susceptibility and state-to-output coupling
